In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the saturation value of the volume integrals is independent of the nature of the projectile.
the saturation values of the volume integrals per pair are about 100 MeVfm3 for nucleon, deuteron, 3He and t, and about 80 MeVfm3 in the alpha-induced reactions.
the systematics of the volume integrals for all the projectiles studied here, including alpha, are consistent with a universal behavior.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the volume integral of the alpha-nuclear optical potential is a universal constant.
there is no evidence for the existence of a saturation value for the volume integral of the alpha-nuclear potential.
the saturation values of the volume integrals per target-projectile pairs of the imaginary part are the same, independent of the mass number and the energy of the projectiles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the saturation value of the volume integral per nucleon is a fundamental quantity of nature, independent of the projectile used.
the systematics in the volume integral of the imaginary part can be understood in terms of the energy dependence of the imaginary part.

the volume integrals for alpha-particle and other light-particle projectiles are very much alike, and the differences in their behavior at low energies are due to the fact that the alpha-nucleon interaction is much weaker than the corresponding interactions for nucleon-nucleon and deuteron-nucleon systems.
